doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Working at The Jug, and bassists Israel Crosby and Wilbur Ware
summary: Williams recalls singing at The Jug where Crosby played bass; Hinton admires Crosby and Wilbur Ware.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I remember working with her at a place called The Jug, I sang from table to table, and split the tips with the guys on the stage, and she was one of the people on the stage. And she could play anything. That was before the old boy with the band got her and took her with his band, and which she stayed with him I think until she died, you know. But, Buckner, or somebody, one of the boys had a band. But she was working playing the piano there, and Israel was playing bass with us for a while.

Israel Crosby, and Wilbur Ware, that’s another bass player from Chicago. These two guys I remember listening to them play. And I always said I wish I had thought of that. Because Israel Crosby played the most beautiful notes.
Yeah, didn’t he? Those things he did with Ahmad Jamal, you know. “Poinciana” and stuff like that that they did together.
He did things before that with Benny Goodman.
